item.title: Open call: Sankofa Heritage Festival opening performance
item.description: Applications have opened for emerging traditional musicians, bands and groups to compete for an opening performance slot at the inaugural Sankofa Heritage Festival, scheduled for 28 February at Carnival City in Johannesburg, South Africa. The festival, founded by South African musician and cultural activist Thandiswa Mazwai, focuses on the preservation and celebration of indigenous African music and cultural heritage. item.title: AFRIMA 2026: All the winners
item.description: Nigerian musicians recorded a strong showing at the ninth All Africa Music Awards (AFRIMA), which concluded in Lagos on 11 January, securing several of the ceremony’s most prominent awards. Burna Boy won Album of the Year for No Sign of Weakness, adding another major accolade to his career. He also shared the Best African Collaboration award with fellow Nigerian artist Shallipopi. item.title: Zim: DJ Nitefreak named Apple Music’s latest Isgubhu cover star
item.description: Zimbabwean DJ and music producer Nitefreak has been unveiled as Apple Music’s latest Isgubhu cover star for January. Known for his deep, hypnotic approach to Afro-house and Afro-tech, Nitefreak has steadily carved out a reputation for immersive, rhythm-driven productions that bridge the underground and the global dance floor. item.title: Open call: Composition Award for women composers in Sweden
item.description: Allmänna Sången in Sweden has announced that submissions for the next Allmänna Sången & Anders Wall Composition Award (ASAWCA) will open in March, ahead of the award presentation in spring 2027. The international competition aims to support and highlight women composers and their contributions to choir music. item.title: Menzi Music stays rooted in tradition on thoughtful Unamagqubu album
item.description: Menzi Music released his maskandi album Unamagqubu on 12 December 2025 through Menzi Music Production. Rooted in traditional guitar-driven arrangements and narrative-led songwriting, the album presents a focused exploration of personal experience and cultural identity within contemporary maskandi. item.title: Open call: National Arts Council support funding programme in SA
item.description: The National Arts Council (NAC) of South Africa has opened applications for its three-year Arts Organisation Support Funding, inviting registered arts organisations and companies to apply for sustained financial support. The funding is open to organisations operating within the disciplines of music, craft, dance, visual arts, literature, theatre and multi-disciplinary arts. item.title: Nigerian music executive Bugwu Aneto-Okeke joins global Merlin board
item.description: Merlin, the global digital music licensing partner for independent labels and distributors, has announced its 2026 Board, bringing together leaders from 12 countries across Africa, Asia, Europe, Latin America, North America, and Oceania. Among the newly elected members is Nigerian music executive Bugwu Aneto-Okeke of Measurable Accurate Digital Solutions (M.A.D Solutions), highlighting Africa’s growing influence in the independent music sector. item.title: Calum Scott returns to SA with Avenoir tour as Cape Town show sells out
item.description: British singer and songwriter Calum Scott has returned to South Africa as part of his global Avenoir Tour, with performances scheduled in Cape Town, Durban and Pretoria. The Cape Town concert, set for 14 January, has sold out, while limited tickets remain available for the Durban show on 16 January and Pretoria on 17 January. item.title: Open call: 2026 UNESCO funding
item.description: UNESCO is inviting national authorities and civil society organisations to submit proposals aimed at strengthening the status of artists and promoting artistic freedom, in line with the 2005 Convention on the Protection and Promotion of the Diversity of Cultural Expressions.
